changes.before: After me Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his chamber.
changes.after: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired a second section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his chamber.
changes.reason: Follows the qere אַחֲרָיו (“after him”) over the ketiv אחרי (“after me”); Nehemiah is not listed among the repairers, and the column follows the qere elsewhere.

changes.before: After me Malchijah, of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the Nethinim and the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the corner.
changes.after: After him Malchijah, of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the Nethinim and the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the corner.
changes.reason: Follows the qere אַחֲרָיו (“after him”) over the ketiv אחרי (“after me”), as in 3:30; the list proceeds section by section from the previous repairer.

changes.before: He said, “What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to avoid the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
changes.after: I said, “What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to avoid the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
changes.reason: Follows the qere וָאוֹמַר (“and I said”) over the ketiv ויאמר; Nehemiah is still the speaker rebuking the nobles, as in 5:7–8 and 5:10.

changes.before: He said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot. While they are still standing there, let them shut the doors and secure them. Appoint watches from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his watch and each opposite his house.”
changes.after: I said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot. While they are still standing there, let them shut the doors and secure them. Appoint watches from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his watch and each opposite his house.”
changes.reason: The Qere וָאֹמַר is first person, “I said” (Nehemiah giving the order, as Rashi reads it); the English made the speaker “he”.

changes.before: “You warned them to turn them back to Your law, but they acted arrogantly and did not listen to Your commandments. They sinned against Your judgments, which a person shall do and live by them. They presented a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks and did not listen.
changes.after: “You warned them to turn them back to Your law, but they acted arrogantly and did not listen to Your commandments. They sinned against Your judgments, which, if a person does them, he shall live by them. They presented a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks and did not listen.
changes.reason: The clause echoing Leviticus 18:5 (אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם וְחָיָה בָהֶם) was hard to follow aloud; recast as a conditional while keeping “live by them”.

changes.before: The two thanksgiving companies stood in the house of God, with me and half the officials with me,
changes.after: The two thanksgiving companies stood in the house of God, and so did I and half the officials with me,
changes.reason: וַאֲנִי וַחֲצִי הַסְּגָנִים עִמִּי makes Nehemiah a second subject who also stood; the doubled “with me” blurred that when read aloud.

changes.before: [BHS 3:6] He considered it beneath him to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him Mordecai’s people. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout Ahasuerus’s kingdom, Mordecai’s people.
changes.after: [BHS 3:6] He considered it beneath him to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him who Mordecai’s people were. Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout Ahasuerus’s kingdom, Mordecai’s people.
changes.reason: הִגִּידוּ לוֹ אֶת־עַם מָרְדֳּכָי means they told him which people Mordecai belonged to; “told him Mordecai’s people” is unclear aloud.

changes.before: I have sinned—what have I done to You, Watcher of humanity? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to myself?
changes.after: If I have sinned, what do I do to You, Watcher of humanity? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to myself?
changes.reason: אֶפְעַל is imperfect (“what do I do”), not past; following Rashi, Job argues that even if he has sinned, it does God no harm.

changes.before: Are not my days few? Let Him cease; let Him turn away from me, so that I may brighten a little,
changes.after: Are not my days few? Cease, and turn away from me, so that I may brighten a little,
changes.reason: The qere וַחֲדָל וְשִׁית are imperatives addressed to God, matching Job’s direct “You” throughout the chapter; the third person followed the ketiv.

changes.before: Look, He may kill me; I have no hope. Yet I will argue my ways before Him.
changes.after: Look, He may kill me; I will hope in Him. Yet I will argue my ways before Him.
changes.reason: The qere לוֹ (“in Him”), followed by the Targum and Rashi, makes this a declaration of hope; the English followed the ketiv לֹא and reversed the meaning.

changes.before: If you say, ‘How we will pursue him!’ and, ‘The root of the matter is found in me,’
changes.after: If you say, ‘How shall we pursue him?’ and, ‘The root of the matter is found in me,’
changes.reason: מַה־נִּרְדָּף־לוֹ is a question (“how shall we pursue him?”, as Rashi reads it), not an exclamation; the exclamation makes the friends sound as if they boast of hounding Job.

changes.before: If you return to Shaddai, you will be built up; put wrongdoing far from your tents.
changes.after: If you return to Shaddai, you will be built up; put wrongdoing far from your tent.
changes.reason: מֵאָהֳלֶךָ is singular, “from your tent”.

changes.before: For I was not cut off before darkness, and He concealed gloom from my face.
changes.after: For I was not cut off before darkness, nor did He conceal gloom from my face.
changes.reason: The negative carries into the second line; Rashi reads it as Job’s complaint that God did not cut him off before the darkness nor hide the gloom from him, whereas the current English says God did conceal it.

changes.before: Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the drawing of wisdom is beyond precious stones.
changes.after: Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the acquiring of wisdom is beyond precious stones.
changes.reason: מֶשֶׁךְ חָכְמָה is the drawing-in, i.e. acquiring, of wisdom (so the classical commentators); “the drawing of wisdom” sounds aloud like a picture.

changes.before: For He loosened His cord and afflicted me, and they cast off the bridle before me.
changes.after: For He loosened my cord and afflicted me, and they cast off the bridle before me.
changes.reason: The Qere יִתְרִי reads “my cord”; the column follows the Qere elsewhere in this chunk (e.g. 21:20, 26:14, 31:20), and the English here followed the Ketiv.

changes.before: Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous, mighty One?
changes.after: Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the righteous and mighty One?
changes.reason: צַדִּיק כַּבִּיר is the object, God as righteous and mighty; with only a comma, the listener hears “mighty One” as a vocative addressed to Job.

changes.before: YHWH restored Job’s fortunes when he prayed for his friend, and YHWH added to everything Job had, doubling it.
changes.after: YHWH restored Job’s fortunes when he prayed for his friends, and YHWH added to everything Job had, doubling it.
changes.reason: רֵעֵהוּ is collective here, referring to the three friends of 42:7–9, so the singular “his friend” misleads a listener.

changes.before: Blessed is the man who has not walked by the counsel of the wicked, stood on the path of sinners, or sat in the seat of scoffers;
changes.after: Blessed is the man who has not walked by the counsel of the wicked, nor stood on the path of sinners, nor sat in the seat of scoffers;
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats לֹא with each of the three verbs; restoring “nor … nor” keeps the triple parallel lines instead of a flattened list.

changes.before: Let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them sing for joy forever, and spread shelter over them. Let those who love Your name exult in You.
changes.after: Let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them sing for joy forever, and may You spread shelter over them. Let those who love Your name exult in You.
changes.reason: וְתָסֵךְ is second person addressed to God (Rashi: You will protect them); without “You” the listener hears the rejoicers as the subject.

changes.before: For day and night Your hand weighed heavily upon me; my moisture was changed by summer's droughts. Selah.
changes.after: For day and night Your hand weighed heavily upon me; my moisture was turned as in the droughts of summer. Selah.
changes.reason: בְּחַרְבֹנֵי קַיִץ is a comparison (“as in the droughts of summer”), as Rashi explains, not the agent of the change; this also removes the straight apostrophe.

changes.before: For it flatters him in his own eyes, toward the finding of his iniquity and hatred.
changes.after: For it flatters him in his own eyes, until his iniquity is found out and hated.
changes.reason: לִמְצֹא עֲוֺנוֹ לִשְׂנֹא are two infinitives (to find his iniquity, to hate), not a noun “hatred”; the flattery lasts until his iniquity is found out and hated, close to Rashi, and the old phrasing was hard to follow aloud.

changes.before: For the wicked will perish; YHWH's enemies are like the fleeting brightness of the plains: they vanish into smoke, they vanish.
changes.after: For the wicked will perish; YHWH's enemies are like the glory of fattened lambs: they vanish into smoke, they vanish.
changes.reason: “Fleeting” is not in the Hebrew, and Rashi reads כִּיקַר כָּרִים as “like the preciousness of fattened lambs” (fattened only for slaughter), which fits the following “vanish into smoke”.

changes.before: Even my trusted companion, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me.
changes.after: Even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me.
changes.reason: אִישׁ שְׁלוֹמִי is “the man of my peace”; “trusted companion, in whom I trusted” doubles a word the Hebrew uses once and loses its image.

changes.before: Even though You rejected us and disgraced us and do not go out with our armies,
changes.after: Yet You have rejected us and disgraced us, and You do not go out with our armies.
changes.reason: אַף here marks the psalm’s turn (“Yet You have rejected us”), a main statement, not a concession leading into the next verse.

changes.before: As we heard, so we have seen in YHWH of hosts' city, in our God's city; God will establish her forever. Selah.
changes.after: As we heard, so we have seen in the city of YHWH of hosts, in our God's city; God will establish her forever. Selah.
changes.reason: “YHWH of hosts’ city” is hard to follow aloud; “the city of YHWH of hosts” follows the Hebrew word order בְּעִיר־יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת.

changes.before: All day my words are grief; all their thoughts against me are for evil.
changes.after: All day they make my words a grief; all their thoughts against me are for evil.
changes.reason: יְעַצֵּבוּ is a plural verb with the enemies as subject (“they grieve my words”), which the English had dropped.

changes.before: Like a snail melting as it goes, like a stillbirth and a mole, they have not seen the sun.
changes.after: Like a snail melting as it goes, like a woman’s stillbirth, they have not seen the sun.
changes.reason: נֵפֶל אֵשֶׁת is one image, “a woman’s stillbirth” (Rashi’s plain sense); the English had added a second item by also rendering the midrashic “mole”.

changes.before: The sin of their mouth is the word of their lips; the poor are trapped through their arrogance, and through the curse and falsehood they recount.
changes.after: The sin of their mouth is the word of their lips; let them be trapped through their arrogance, and through the curse and falsehood they recount.
changes.reason: וְיִלָּכְדוּ בִגְאוֹנָם has the enemies as subject (“let them be caught in their pride”); there is no “poor” in the verse.

changes.before: You gave those who fear You a trial to be tested, for the sake of beauty. Selah.
changes.after: You gave those who fear You a trial to be tested, for the sake of truth. Selah.
changes.reason: קֹשֶׁט means “truth” (as Targum קושטא and Rashi take it), not “beauty”.

changes.before: God spoke in His sanctuary: I will exult; I will divide a portion, and measure the Valley of Succoth.
changes.after: God spoke in His sanctuary: I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and measure the Valley of Succoth.
changes.reason: שְׁכֶם here is the place name Shechem, parallel to the Valley of Succoth (as the column renders it in the twin verse, Psalm 108).

changes.before: Moab is my washbasin; upon Edom I will cast my lock; Philistia, join yourself to me.
changes.after: Moab is my washbasin; upon Edom I will cast my sandal; Philistia, join yourself to me.
changes.reason: נַעֲלִי is “my sandal” (as the column renders it in Psalm 108), not “my lock”.

changes.before: God cast them down; an arrow—suddenly their wounds came.
changes.after: God shot them with an arrow; suddenly their wounds came.
changes.reason: וַיֹּרֵם אֱלֹהִים חֵץ is “God shot them with an arrow” (Rashi), answering their own shooting in vv. 4–5; “cast them down” lost the image.

changes.before: Sing to God; make music to His name. Praise Him who rides in the heavens by His name Yah, and exult before Him.
changes.after: Sing to God; make music to His name. Praise Him who rides in the heavens—Yah is His name—and exult before Him.
changes.reason: בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ means “Yah is His name”; “rides … by His name Yah” sounds aloud as if He rides by means of the name.

changes.before: Gifts will come from Egypt; Cush will hasten its hands toward God.
changes.after: Nobles will come from Egypt; Cush will hasten its hands toward God.
changes.reason: חַשְׁמַנִּים are nobles or princes (Targum and Rashi), not gifts.

changes.before: For envy concerning Your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those reproaching You have fallen on me.
changes.after: For zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those reproaching You have fallen on me.
changes.reason: קִנְאַת בֵּיתְךָ is zeal for God’s house (Rashi), not envy.

changes.before: May he live, and may He give him some of Sheba’s gold; may He pray for him continually, and bless him all day.
changes.after: May he live, and may he give him some of Sheba’s gold; may he pray for him continually, and bless him all day.
changes.reason: The subjects are human (Rashi: the king gives the rescued poor man gold, and the poor man prays for the king); capital “He” made God the one who prays for the king.

changes.before: When I considered how to know this, it appeared injustice in my eyes,
changes.after: When I considered how to know this, it was toil in my eyes,
changes.reason: עָמָל is toil or trouble (“it was a weariness in my eyes”), not injustice.

changes.before: Like a dream without awakening, Lord, in the city You will despise their image.
changes.after: Like a dream upon awakening, Lord, in the city You will despise their image.
changes.reason: כַּחֲלוֹם מֵהָקִיץ is a dream that vanishes once one wakes (Rashi); “without awakening” reverses the image.

changes.before: With Your counsel You led me, and afterward You took me for glory.
changes.after: With Your counsel You guide me, and afterward You will take me for glory.
changes.reason: Both verbs are imperfect (תַנְחֵנִי, תִּקָּחֵנִי), a present-future confidence that the past tense obscured.

changes.before: But for me, God’s nearness is good; I have set my refuge in Lord YHWH, to recount all Your messages.
changes.after: But for me, God’s nearness is good; I have set my refuge in Lord YHWH, to recount all Your works.
changes.reason: מַלְאֲכוֹתֶיךָ is from מְלָאכָה, “work”, not from מַלְאָךְ, “messenger”.

changes.before: Why do You draw back Your hand, Your right hand? Bring it out from within Your bosom!
changes.after: Why do You draw back Your hand, Your right hand? Bring it out from within Your bosom and consume them!
changes.reason: The verse ends with כַלֵּה, “consume/destroy” (Rashi: take it out and destroy them), which the English had omitted.

changes.before: My voice goes to God, and I cry out; my voice goes to God—give ear to me!
changes.after: My voice goes to God, and I cry out; my voice goes to God, and He will give ear to me.
changes.reason: וְהַאֲזִין is pointed as a perfect with vav (“and He will give ear”), a statement of confidence about God, not an imperative to Him.

changes.before: The skies poured streams of thick waters; the skies gave voice; Your arrows too went about.
changes.after: The clouds poured out water; the skies gave voice; Your arrows too went about.
changes.reason: In זֹרְמוּ מַיִם עָבוֹת the clouds (עָבוֹת) are the subject that pours water; “thick waters” misread the noun, and “skies” belongs to the next clause.

changes.before: A human ate the bread of mighty ones; He sent them provision to satisfaction.
changes.after: Each man ate the bread of mighty ones; He sent them provision to satisfaction.
changes.reason: אִישׁ here is distributive (“each one”, so Rashi), not “a human”; the old wording reads as if a single person ate.

changes.before: He leveled a path for His anger; He did not spare their soul from death, and handed their body over to pestilence.
changes.after: He leveled a path for His anger; He did not spare their soul from death, and handed their life over to pestilence.
changes.reason: חַיָּתָם is “their life” (parallel to נַפְשָׁם), not “their body”.

changes.before: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, rouse Your might; it is for You to save us.
changes.after: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, rouse Your might, and come to save us.
changes.reason: וּלְכָה is the imperative “and come” (Rashi, Ibn Ezra); “it is for You” drops the plea and misreads the verb.

changes.before: You fed them bread of tears and gave them tears to drink by the shalish.
changes.after: You fed them bread of tears and gave them tears to drink by the measure.
changes.reason: The untranslated “shalish” is opaque aloud; Rashi explains שָׁלִישׁ as a measuring vessel.

changes.before: You make us an object of strife for our neighbors, and our enemies mock them.
changes.after: You make us an object of strife for our neighbors, and our enemies mock among themselves.
changes.reason: יִלְעֲגוּ־לָמוֹ is “mock to themselves”; “mock them” wrongly makes the neighbours the object of the mockery.

changes.before: I removed his shoulder from the burden; his palms passed away from the cooking pot.
changes.after: I removed his shoulder from the burden; his palms were freed from the basket.
changes.reason: “Passed away” sounds like dying aloud; תַּעֲבֹרְנָה means were released, and Rashi takes דּוּד as the clay-carrying basket of Egyptian labour.

changes.before: Know that YHWH—He is God. He made us, and not we; His people and the flock of His pasture.
changes.after: Know that YHWH—He is God. He made us, and we are His; His people and the flock of His pasture.
changes.reason: Follows the qere וְלוֹ (“and we are His”), as Rashi and the Targum read, instead of the ketiv “and not we”, which also leaves the clause dangling.

changes.before: He weakened his strength on the way; He shortened my days.
changes.after: He weakened my strength on the way; He shortened my days.
changes.reason: Follows the qere כֹּחִי (“my strength”), matching “my days” in the same line, as the column does elsewhere with qere readings.

changes.before: The sun rises; they gather away and lie down in their dens.
changes.after: The sun rises; they withdraw and lie down in their dens.
changes.reason: “Gather away” trips the ear; יֵאָסֵפוּן here means the beasts withdraw (are gathered in) to their dens.

changes.before: He asked, and He brought quail; He satisfied them with bread from heaven.
changes.after: They asked, and He brought quail; He satisfied them with bread from heaven.
changes.reason: The one who asked (שָׁאַל) is the people, as Rashi explains, not God; “He asked” made God the asker.

changes.before: for they embittered his spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips.
changes.after: for they rebelled against His spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips.
changes.reason: הִמְרוּ is “rebelled”, the same verb as in vv. 7 and 43, and Rashi takes “his spirit” as God’s spirit.

changes.before: They rejoiced because they were quiet, and He guided them to their desired haven.
changes.after: They rejoiced because the waves were quiet, and He guided them to their desired haven.
changes.reason: Aloud “they were quiet” sounds like the sailors; the subject of יִשְׁתֹּקוּ is the waves of v. 29, as Rashi explains.

changes.before: For a wicked mouth and a deceitful mouth have opened against me; they speak with me with a lying tongue.
changes.after: For a wicked mouth and a deceitful mouth have opened against me; they speak to me with a lying tongue.
changes.reason: “With me with” trips the ear; “to me” keeps the sense of דִּבְּרוּ אִתִּי.

changes.before: The sum of Your word is truth, and every righteous judgment of Yours is forever.
changes.after: The beginning of Your word is truth, and every righteous judgment of Yours is forever.
changes.reason: רֹאשׁ דְּבָרְךָ is “the head/beginning of Your word”; Rashi reads it as the first words spoken at Sinai, shown true by what followed, so “beginning” keeps the source’s image rather than “sum”.

changes.before: For there is not a word on my tongue— look, YHWH, You know it all.
changes.after: For while there is not yet a word on my tongue, look, YHWH, You know it all.
changes.reason: Aloud “there is not a word on my tongue” sounds like speechlessness; the classical commentators read כִּי אֵין מִלָּה as “before a word is on my tongue You already know it all”.

changes.before: And I said, “Surely darkness will overwhelm me, and night will be light around me.”
changes.after: And I said, “Surely darkness will overwhelm me,” but night is light around me.
changes.reason: Only the first line is what the psalmist says; וְלַיְלָה אוֹר בַּעֲדֵנִי is the answer (night itself is light around me, as Rashi and v. 12 show), so it must not sit inside the quotation.

changes.before: Let your eyes look straight ahead, and your eyelids direct themselves before you.
changes.after: Let your eyes look straight ahead, and your eyelids gaze straight before you.
changes.reason: יַיְשִׁרוּ means the eyelids look straight ahead; “direct themselves” is hard to follow aloud.

changes.before: She turns him aside with her many persuasions; with her lips' smoothness she drives him away.
changes.after: She turns him aside with her many persuasions; with her lips' smoothness she lures him away.
changes.reason: תַּדִּיחֶנּוּ here means she entices or leads him astray (Rashi: she seduces him); “drives him away” says the opposite.

changes.before: One who disciplines a scoffer takes disgrace for himself, and one who reproves a wicked person—his blemish.
changes.after: One who disciplines a scoffer takes disgrace for himself, and one who reproves a wicked person gets himself a blemish.
changes.reason: Supplies the verb carried over from the first line so the elliptical “his blemish” is understood aloud as falling on the reprover, as Rashi reads it.

changes.before: One who keeps discipline is a path to life, but one who abandons reproof leads astray.
changes.after: One who keeps discipline is on a path to life, but one who abandons reproof leads astray.
changes.reason: The Hebrew sets “a path to life” beside the one who keeps discipline; read aloud, the English made the person himself a path.

changes.before: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and one who takes lives is wise.
changes.after: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and one who wins souls is wise.
changes.reason: לֹקֵחַ נְפָשׂוֹת means one who gains or wins people (Rashi: draws them to good); in English “takes lives” means kills.

changes.before: Overthrow the wicked, and they are no more, but the house of the righteous will stand.
changes.after: The wicked are overthrown and are no more, but the house of the righteous will stand.
changes.reason: הָפוֹךְ is an infinitive absolute stating what happens to the wicked, not a command to the listener.

changes.before: Walk with the wise and become wise, but one who companions with fools will fare badly.
changes.after: One who walks with the wise will become wise, but one who companions with fools will fare badly.
changes.reason: Follows the Qere הוֹלֵךְ … יֶחְכָּם (as read in the synagogue), which also matches the second line’s “one who companions with fools.”

changes.before: Before breaking a man's heart grows high, and before honor comes humility.
changes.after: Before breaking, a man's heart grows high, and before honor comes humility.
changes.reason: Without a pause, “before breaking a man’s heart” is heard as one phrase about breaking someone’s heart; the comma keeps “before breaking” as its own phrase, as in 16:18.

changes.before: A guilty man's way is twisted, but the pure person's work is upright.
changes.after: A man’s way is twisted and strange, but the pure person’s work is upright.
changes.reason: וָזָר is “and strange” (estranged), as Rashi and the classical Jewish commentators read it; “guilty” rests on an Arabic cognate and turns the pair of adjectives into a different subject.

changes.before: When your enemies fall, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles, do not let your heart exult,
changes.after: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles, do not let your heart exult,
changes.reason: The Qere אוֹיִבְךָ is singular, and the verse goes on “when he stumbles”; the plural follows only the Ketiv and jars with “he”.

changes.before: Men of blood hate a blameless person, but the upright seek his life.
changes.after: Men of blood hate a blameless person, but the upright seek his welfare.
changes.reason: In English “seek his life” means to try to kill him, the opposite of the contrast; the classical Jewish commentators read the upright as seeking the blameless man’s good.

changes.before: Had YHWH of hosts not left us a very small remnant, we would have become like Sodom, resembled Gomorrah.
changes.after: Had YHWH of hosts not left us a very small remnant, we would have become like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.
changes.reason: The second line of the parallel (לַעֲמֹרָה דָּמִינוּ) has its own verb; giving it a subject keeps the couplet and stops the clipped “resembled Gomorrah” from tripping the ear.

changes.before: Learn to do good, seek justice, set the oppressor right. Judge for the orphan, plead for the widow.
changes.after: Learn to do good, seek justice, relieve the oppressed. Judge for the orphan, plead for the widow.
changes.reason: חָמוֹץ is ambiguous; Rashi explains it as the one who is robbed and Targum renders “vindicate the wronged,” so the object is the oppressed, not the oppressor.

changes.before: when the Lord has washed away the filth of Zion's daughters and rinses Jerusalem's bloodshed from her midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
changes.after: when the Lord has washed away the filth of Zion's daughters and has rinsed Jerusalem's bloodshed from her midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
changes.reason: Both verbs describe the same completed cleansing; matching “has washed … and has rinsed” avoids a tense jolt when read aloud.

changes.before: who acquit the wicked for a bribe and take the righteous ones' right away from him!
changes.after: who acquit the wicked for a bribe and take away the right of the righteous from each of them!
changes.reason: “The righteous ones’ right away from him” is hard to hear (ones’/right/him); the Hebrew’s distributive singular מִמֶּנּוּ is kept as “from each of them.”

changes.before: Yet today he will stand at Nob, shaking his hand toward the mountain of the house of Zion, Jerusalem's hill.
changes.after: Yet today he will stand at Nob, shaking his hand toward the mountain of Daughter Zion, Jerusalem's hill.
changes.reason: The column follows the qere elsewhere, and here the qere is בַּת־צִיּוֹן (“Daughter Zion”), not the ketiv בית (“house”); it also matches “Daughter Gallim” in 10:30.

changes.before: The poorest of the poor will graze, and the needy lie down securely. I will kill your root with famine, and he will slay your remnant.
changes.after: The firstborn of the poor will graze, and the needy lie down securely. I will kill your root with famine, and he will slay your remnant.
changes.reason: בְּכוֹרֵי דַלִּים is “the firstborn of the poor”; keeping the source’s image (which Rashi applies to Israel) rather than flattening it to a superlative.

changes.before: He cried, “A lion! On the watchtower, Lord, I stand continually by day; at my post I remain through all the nights.
changes.after: He cried out like a lion, “On the watchtower, Lord, I stand continually by day; at my post I remain through all the nights.
changes.reason: Following Rashi, the watchman calls out like a lion; “A lion!” sounds aloud as if a lion had been sighted, which the Hebrew does not report.

changes.before: Thus says the Lord YHWH of hosts: “Go, enter to this steward, to Shebna who is over the house:
changes.after: Thus says the Lord YHWH of hosts: “Go, go in to this steward, to Shebna who is over the house:
changes.reason: “Enter to this steward” trips the ear; “go in to” keeps the Hebrew’s two verbs of motion (לֶךְ־בֹּא) in natural English.

changes.before: For You have made a city a heap, a fortified town a ruin, a foreigners' palace no city; it will never be rebuilt.
changes.after: For You have made a city a heap, a fortified town a ruin, a foreigners' palace no longer a city; it will never be rebuilt.
changes.reason: מֵעִיר means the palace is no longer a city; “a foreigners’ palace no city” is hard to follow when heard.

changes.before: Like heat in a dry place, You will subdue the foreigners' din; like heat under a cloud's shade, the ruthless ones' cutting down will be answered in song.
changes.after: Like heat in a dry place, You will subdue the foreigners' din; like heat under a cloud's shade, the song of the ruthless will be brought low.
changes.reason: Following Rashi, זְמִיר is “song” and יַעֲנֶה “will be humbled”: the tyrants’ song is silenced, parallel to the subdued din of foreigners; the current wording says the opposite kind of thing.

changes.before: Therefore thus says YHWH, who redeemed Abraham, concerning Jacob's house: “Jacob will no longer be ashamed, nor will his face now grow pale,
changes.after: Therefore thus says YHWH, who redeemed Abraham, concerning Jacob's house: “Jacob will not now be ashamed, nor will his face now grow pale,
changes.reason: The Hebrew repeats לֹא עַתָּה (“not now”) in both lines; restoring the repetition keeps the parallelism.

changes.before: Turn aside from the way, bend us away from the path; remove Israel's Holy One from before us.”
changes.after: Turn aside from the way, bend away from the path; remove Israel's Holy One from before us.”
changes.reason: הַטּוּ מִנֵּי־אֹרַח has no “us”: the people tell the seers themselves to turn off the path, as in the parallel line.

changes.before: For thus says the Lord YHWH, Israel's Holy One: “In tranquility and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust will be your strength.” But you were unwilling.
changes.after: For thus says the Lord YHWH, Israel's Holy One: “In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust will be your strength.” But you were unwilling.
changes.reason: בְּשׁוּבָה is “in returning”; Targum and Rashi read it as returning to God, which “tranquility” loses.

changes.before: Every place the established staff passed, upon which YHWH brings rest, will have tambourines and lyres; with battles of waving He will fight against her.
changes.after: Every place the established staff passed, upon which YHWH brings rest, will have tambourines and lyres; with battles of waving He will fight against them.
changes.reason: The column follows the qere, and the qere here is בָּם (“against them”), not the ketiv בה (“against her”).

changes.before: Righteousness's work will be peace, and righteousness's service quietness and confidence forever.
changes.after: The work of righteousness will be peace, and the service of righteousness quietness and confidence forever.
changes.reason: “Righteousness’s” twice is a tongue-twister aloud; the “of” phrasing keeps the same wording and the repeated “righteousness”.

changes.before: My generation was uprooted and taken from me like a shepherd’s tent. Like a weaver I cut off my life. He will strip me of my glory. By day and by night, You bring me to an end.
changes.after: My generation was uprooted and taken from me like a shepherd’s tent. Like a weaver I cut off my life. From the loom He cuts me off. By day and by night, You bring me to an end.
changes.reason: מִדַּלָּה יְבַצְּעֵנִי is “from the thrum/loom He cuts me off” (Ibn Ezra, Radak), continuing the weaver image; nothing in the Hebrew means “glory” (Rashi reads dallah as wasting sickness).

changes.before: Like a swift and a crane I chatter; like a dove I moan. My eyes are lifted on high. Lord, seize me; stand surety for me!
changes.after: Like a swift and a crane I chatter; like a dove I moan. My eyes are lifted on high. Lord, I am oppressed; stand surety for me!
changes.reason: עָשְׁקָה־לִּי means “oppression is upon me / I am oppressed,” not a plea for God to seize him.

changes.before: Hezekiah said, “What a sign, that I will go up to YHWH's house!”
changes.after: Hezekiah said, “What is the sign that I will go up to YHWH's house?”
changes.reason: מָה אוֹת is a question asking for the sign (cf. 2 Kgs 20:8), not an exclamation.

changes.before: Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear YHWH of hosts' word:
changes.after: Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of YHWH of hosts:
changes.reason: “YHWH of hosts' word” trips the ear; the of-phrase reads aloud clearly with no change of sense.

changes.before: Grass dries and a flower fades because YHWH's breath blows upon it. Surely the people are grass.
changes.after: The grass withers and the flower fades because YHWH's breath blows upon it. Surely the people are grass.
changes.reason: יָבֵשׁ חָצִיר נָבֵל צִיץ is repeated verbatim in v. 8; render it identically so the deliberate refrain is kept.

changes.before: Who measured water by His stride, gauged the heavens with a span, measured the earth's dust by thirds, and weighed mountains on a scale and hills in balances?
changes.after: Who measured water in the hollow of His hand, gauged the heavens with a span, measured the earth's dust by thirds, and weighed mountains on a scale and hills in balances?
changes.reason: שֹׁעַל is the hollow of the hand / a handful (cf. 1 Kgs 20:10), not a stride; it pairs with the span (זֶרֶת).

changes.before: Lift up your eyes and see: Who created these? He brings out their host by number and calls each one by name. Because of His great might and strength, not one is missing.
changes.after: Lift up your eyes on high and see: Who created these? He brings out their host by number and calls each one by name. Because of His great might and strength, not one is missing.
changes.reason: Restores omitted מָרוֹם “on high.”

changes.before: But now thus says YHWH, your Creator, Jacob, and your Former, Israel: “Do not fear, for I redeemed you. I called you by your name; you are Mine.
changes.after: But now thus says YHWH, your Creator, Jacob, and the One who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I redeemed you. I called you by your name; you are Mine.
changes.reason: “Your Former” is heard as the adjective “former”; “the One who formed you” keeps וְיֹצֶרְךָ and matches 44:2.

changes.before: Do not fear or be dismayed. Did I not let you hear and declare it long ago? You are My witnesses. Is there a God apart from Me? There is no rock I do not know.”
changes.after: Do not fear or be dismayed. Did I not let you hear and declare it long ago? You are My witnesses. Is there a God apart from Me? There is no rock; I know of none.”
changes.reason: וְאֵין צוּר בַּל־יָדָעְתִּי denies any other rock (“I know none”); the old wording meant God knows every rock.

changes.before: A deceived heart has turned him toward a shepherd of ashes. He cannot rescue his life or say, ‘Is there not a lie in my right hand?’
changes.after: He feeds on ashes; a deceived heart has turned him aside. He cannot rescue his life or say, ‘Is there not a lie in my right hand?’
changes.reason: רֹעֶה אֵפֶר describes the idol-maker himself (he grazes on ashes), and הִטָּהוּ means “led him astray,” not toward another figure.

changes.before: Thus says YHWH, Israel's Holy One and its Former: “Ask Me about the coming signs; would you command Me concerning My sons and the work of My hands?
changes.after: Thus says YHWH, Israel's Holy One and the One who formed it: “Ask Me about the things to come; would you command Me concerning My sons and the work of My hands?
changes.reason: הָאֹתִיּוֹת means “the coming things” (as rendered in 41:23, 44:7), not “signs”; “its Former” also misleads aloud.

changes.before: ‘Only to me did He promise righteousness and strength in YHWH.’ To Him people will come, and all who rage against Him will be ashamed.
changes.after: ‘Only in YHWH,’ one will say, ‘do I have righteousness and strength.’ To Him people will come, and all who rage against Him will be ashamed.
changes.reason: אַךְ qualifies בַּיהוָה (only in YHWH), and this is the confession of the swearing tongue of v. 23 (cf. Rashi), not a promise made only to the speaker.

changes.before: Bel crouches; Nebo soils himself. Their idols have become like wild and domestic animals; what you carry weighs heavily, a load for the weary.
changes.after: Bel crouches; Nebo soils himself. Their idols are loaded on wild and domestic animals; what you carry weighs heavily, a load for the weary.
changes.reason: הָיוּ עֲצַבֵּיהֶם לַחַיָּה וְלַבְּהֵמָה means the idols have become loads for the beasts (Rashi), as the rest of the verse shows, not that they resemble animals.

changes.before: I call a counselor from the east, from a distant land the man of My counsel. Indeed, I spoke; I will also bring it about. I formed it; I will also do it.
changes.after: I call a bird of prey from the east, from a distant land the man of My counsel. Indeed, I spoke; I will also bring it about. I formed it; I will also do it.
changes.reason: עַיִט is a bird of prey (Rashi: swift as a bird), not a counselor; “the man of My counsel” is the parallel line.

changes.before: You said, ‘I will be mistress forever,’ until you no longer took these things to heart or remembered their outcome.
changes.after: You said, ‘I will be mistress forever,’ so that you did not take these things to heart or remember their outcome.
changes.reason: עַד לֹא־שַׂמְתְּ says she never laid these to heart; “no longer” implies she once had.

changes.before: They are created now, not long ago; I let you hear before their day, and you had not heard them before, lest you say, ‘Look, I knew them.’
changes.after: They are created now, not long ago; before today you had not heard them, lest you say, ‘Look, I knew them.’
changes.reason: וְלִפְנֵי־יוֹם וְלֹא שְׁמַעְתָּם means “before today you did not hear them”; the added “I let you hear before their day” contradicts the verse.

changes.before: Look, I refined you, but not as silver; I chose for you the crucible of poverty.
changes.after: Look, I refined you, but not as silver; I tested you in the crucible of poverty.
changes.reason: בְּחַרְתִּיךָ has Israel as object (“you”), in the crucible; Rashi glosses it as בְּחַנְתִּיךָ “I tested you,” matching “refined.”

changes.before: Thus says YHWH: “At a time of favor I answered you, and on a day of salvation I helped you. I will guard you and appoint you as a covenant people, to establish a land and apportion desolate inheritances,
changes.after: Thus says YHWH: “At a time of favor I answered you, and on a day of salvation I helped you. I will guard you and appoint you as a covenant for the people, to establish a land and apportion desolate inheritances,
changes.reason: לִבְרִית עָם is “a covenant for the people,” as the column renders the same phrase in 42:6.

changes.before: to say to prisoners, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ They will graze along roads, with pasture beside every stream.
changes.after: to say to prisoners, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ They will graze along roads, and on all bare heights will be their pasture.
changes.reason: שְׁפָיִים are bare heights (so the column at 41:18), not streams.

changes.before: I will give your taunters' flesh as food, and drinkers of blood will become drunk on their blood as on sweet wine. All flesh will know that I am YHWH, your Savior and Redeemer, Jacob's Mighty One.”
changes.after: I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they will be drunk on their own blood as on sweet wine. All flesh will know that I am YHWH, your Savior and Redeemer, Jacob's Mighty One.”
changes.reason: וְהַאֲכַלְתִּי אֶת־מוֹנַיִךְ אֶת־בְּשָׂרָם: the oppressors are made to eat their own flesh and get drunk on their own blood; “drinkers of blood” is an added subject.

changes.before: For YHWH has comforted Zion and all her ruins. He makes her wilderness like Eden and her wasteland like YHWH's garden. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and a voice of song.
changes.after: For YHWH has comforted Zion; He has comforted all her ruins. He makes her wilderness like Eden and her wasteland like YHWH's garden. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and a voice of song.
changes.reason: Keeps the repeated נִחַם, which the Hebrew states twice.

changes.before: May YHWH's ransomed return and come to Zion with singing, everlasting joy upon their heads. May gladness and joy overtake them; may sorrow and sighing flee.
changes.after: YHWH's ransomed will return and come to Zion with singing, everlasting joy upon their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them; sorrow and sighing will flee.
changes.reason: יְשׁוּבוּן / יַשִּׂיגוּן / נָסוּ are indicative promises (as in 35:10), not wishes.

changes.before: All you beasts of the field, come to devour all the beasts in the forest!
changes.after: All you beasts of the field, come and devour, all you beasts in the forest!
changes.reason: כָּל־חַיְתוֹ בַּיָּעַר is a second vocative parallel to the first line; the beasts are summoned, not devoured.

changes.before: On whom do you depend for your delights? Against whom do you open your mouth wide and stretch out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, offspring of falsehood?
changes.after: Over whom do you make sport? Against whom do you open your mouth wide and stretch out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, offspring of falsehood?
changes.reason: הִתְעַנֵּג עַל here means to make sport of someone (Rashi: whom are you mocking and jesting at?), not to depend on someone for delights.

changes.before: You brought oil as a gift to the king and multiplied your perfumes. You sent your envoys far away and brought others low to Sheol.
changes.after: You brought oil as a gift to the king and multiplied your perfumes. You sent your envoys far away and brought them low, even to Sheol.
changes.reason: The Hebrew has no “others”: וַתַּשְׁפִּילִי continues the sending of the envoys, sunk as low as Sheol.

changes.before: Because of his sinful theft I was angry and struck him. I hid Myself in anger because he went rebelliously along his heart's way.
changes.after: Because of the iniquity of his greed I was angry and struck him. I hid Myself in anger, yet he went on rebelliously along his heart's way.
changes.reason: בֶּצַע is greed or unjust gain, not theft, and וַיֵּלֶךְ שׁוֹבָב says he kept straying despite the blow, not that his straying was the reason for God’s hiding.

changes.before: If you turn back your foot because of the Sabbath, from doing your own affairs on My holy day, call the Sabbath a delight and YHWH's holy day honored, and honor it by avoiding your own ways, pursuing your own affairs, and speaking your own business,
changes.after: If you turn back your foot because of the Sabbath, from doing your own affairs on My holy day, call the Sabbath a delight and YHWH's holy day honored, and honor it by refraining from your own ways, from pursuing your own affairs, and from speaking your own business,
changes.reason: Read aloud, “avoiding … pursuing … speaking” sounds as if pursuing and speaking are commanded; repeating “from”, as the Hebrew repeats מִן, keeps all three under the refraining.

changes.before: Then you will see and shine; your heart will tremble and grow wide, for the west's abundance will turn toward you, and the nations' wealth will come to you.
changes.after: Then you will see and shine; your heart will tremble and grow wide, for the abundance of the sea will turn toward you, and the nations' wealth will come to you.
changes.reason: הֲמוֹן יָם is “the abundance of the sea”; “the west” replaces the source’s image with an interpretation.

changes.before: Your people will all be righteous; they will inherit the land forever, a shoot of His planting, the work of My hands, for displaying glory.
changes.after: Your people will all be righteous; they will inherit the land forever, a shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, for displaying glory.
changes.reason: Read with the Qere מַטָּעַי (“My planting”), which also matches the parallel “the work of My hands”; the English followed the Ketiv.

changes.before: In exchange for your double shame and the disgrace they lamented as their lot, they will therefore inherit double in their land; everlasting joy will be theirs.
changes.after: Instead of your shame, a double portion; instead of disgrace, they will shout for joy over their lot. Therefore in their land they will inherit double; everlasting joy will be theirs.
changes.reason: יָרֹנּוּ means “they will shout for joy”, not “lamented”, and מִשְׁנֶה is the double portion that replaces the shame (Rashi), not a “double shame”.

changes.before: In all their distress He did not distress them, and the angel of His presence saved them. In His love and pity He redeemed them, lifted them, and carried them throughout the days of old.
changes.after: In all their distress He was distressed, and the angel of His presence saved them. In His love and pity He redeemed them, lifted them, and carried them throughout the days of old.
changes.reason: Following the Qere לוֹ צָר with Rashi and Targum: God shared in their distress; the English rendered the Ketiv לֹא in a way that reverses the verse’s comfort.

changes.before: His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: Where is the one who brought them up from the sea, as a shepherd his flock? Where is the one who placed His holy spirit within them,
changes.after: His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: Where is the one who brought them up from the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is the one who placed His holy spirit within them,
changes.reason: אֵת רֹעֵי צֹאנוֹ means “with the shepherds of His flock” (Rashi: Moses and Aaron); “as a shepherd his flock” adds a simile and drops the shepherds.

changes.before: Like animals spreading out in a valley, YHWH's spirit guided them. So You led Your people to make Yourself a glorious name.
changes.after: Like cattle going down into a valley, YHWH's spirit guided them. So You led Your people to make Yourself a glorious name.
changes.reason: תֵרֵד is “goes down”; the source’s picture is a herd descending gently into the valley, not spreading out.

changes.before: You struck down the one rejoicing and doing righteousness, those who remembered You in Your ways. Look, You were angry because we sinned; through them we had long been saved.
changes.after: You met the one rejoicing and doing righteousness, those who remembered You in Your ways. Look, You were angry because we sinned; through them we had long been saved.
changes.reason: פָּגַעְתָּ here is meeting with favor (Rashi, Ibn Ezra), not striking down; the English reversed the sense of the verse.

changes.before: No one calls on Your name or rouses himself to hold fast to You, for You hid Your face from us and made us wander in the power of our iniquities.
changes.after: No one calls on Your name or rouses himself to hold fast to You, for You hid Your face from us and made us melt away in the power of our iniquities.
changes.reason: וַתְּמוּגֵנוּ is from מוג, “melt”; “wander” loses the source’s image.

changes.before: Hear YHWH's word, you who tremble at His word! Your brothers who hate you and cast you out said, ‘For my name's sake let YHWH be glorified!’ And we will see your joy, but they will be ashamed.
changes.after: Hear YHWH's word, you who tremble at His word! Your brothers who hate you and cast you out for My name’s sake said, ‘Let YHWH be glorified, and let us see your joy!’ But they will be ashamed.
changes.reason: “For My name’s sake” tells why they cast you out (God is speaking), and “let us see your joy” belongs to their mocking words (Rashi); the English put “my name” in the brothers’ mouths.

changes.before: so that you may nurse and be satisfied from her consoling breast, so that you may drink deeply and delight in her approaching glory.
changes.after: so that you may nurse and be satisfied from her consoling breast, so that you may drink deeply and delight in the radiance of her glory.
changes.reason: Rashi explains מִזִּיז as מִזִּיו, “from the radiance”; “approaching” has no basis in the Hebrew.

changes.before: For long ago I broke your yoke and tore apart your bonds, but you said, I will not serve. On every high hill and beneath every leafy tree you sprawled as a prostitute.
changes.after: For long ago I broke your yoke and tore apart your bonds, and you said, I will not transgress. Yet on every high hill and beneath every leafy tree you sprawled as a prostitute.
changes.reason: Read with the Qere אֶעֱבוֹר (“I will not transgress”) as Rashi does: Israel promised not to transgress, and the next clause shows the promise broken.

changes.before: I will smash them against one another, fathers and sons together—YHWH's declaration. I will not pity or spare or have compassion, keeping Me from destroying them.
changes.after: I will smash them against one another, fathers and sons together—YHWH's declaration. I will not pity or spare or have compassion so as not to destroy them.
changes.reason: מֵהַשְׁחִיתָם means “so as not to destroy them”; “keeping Me from destroying them” is hard to follow aloud and sounds as if something restrains God.

changes.before: Say to the king and the queen mother: Humble yourselves and sit down, for your head-ornament has come down, your splendid crown.
changes.after: Say to the king and the queen mother: Humble yourselves and sit down, for your splendid crown has come down from your heads.
changes.reason: Rashi and the Targum read מַרְאֲשֹׁתֵיכֶם as “from your heads”, the place the crown falls from, not a second ornament.

changes.before: What will you say when He attends to you, when you yourself taught them to be intimates over you as head? Will not pains seize you like a woman giving birth?
changes.after: What will you say when He attends to you, when you yourself taught them, as your close friends, to be head over you? Will not pains seize you like a woman giving birth?
changes.reason: The phrase “to be intimates over you as head” is hard to follow aloud; following Rashi (the allies she courted as friends become her masters), the order is clarified without changing the sense.

changes.before: I will deliver you from the wicked's hand and redeem you from the ruthless one's grasp.
changes.after: I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.
changes.reason: עָרִצִים is plural (“the ruthless”), not a single ruthless one; the phrasing also reads more easily aloud.

changes.before: if that nation turns from the evil concerning which I spoke against it, I will relent concerning the disaster I planned to do to it.
changes.after: if that nation against which I spoke turns from its evil, I will relent concerning the disaster I planned to do to it.
changes.reason: מֵרָעָתוֹ is “from its evil”, and אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתִּי עָלָיו refers to the nation God spoke against, not to its evil.

changes.before: House of David, thus says YHWH: Administer justice in the morning and rescue the robbed from the oppressor's hand, lest My fury go out like fire and burn with no one to quench it because of the evil of their deeds.
changes.after: House of David, thus says YHWH: Administer justice in the morning and rescue the robbed from the oppressor's hand, lest My fury go out like fire and burn with no one to quench it because of the evil of your deeds.
changes.reason: The qere מַעַלְלֵיכֶם (“your deeds”), which the column follows elsewhere, fits the direct address to the house of David.

changes.before: You who dwell in Lebanon and nest among the cedars, how gracious you will be when pangs come upon you, anguish like a woman giving birth!
changes.after: You who dwell in Lebanon and nest among the cedars, how you will groan when pangs come upon you, anguish like a woman giving birth!
changes.reason: מַה־נֵּחַנְתְּ does not mean “how gracious you will be”; the Targum renders it “how you will groan” (Rashi similarly: how you will plead), which fits the birth-pangs image.

changes.before: But like the bad figs, too bad to eat—for thus says YHWH—so I will make Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, Jerusalem's remnant left in this land, and those dwelling in Egypt's land.
changes.after: But like the bad figs, too bad to eat—for thus says YHWH—so I will give up Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, Jerusalem's remnant left in this land, and those dwelling in Egypt's land.
changes.reason: “So I will make Zedekiah …” ends the verse without saying what he is made; כֵּן אֶתֵּן is “so will I give up”, as the Targum (כֵּן אֶמְסַר) has it, which is complete when heard.

changes.before: Flee from Babylon's midst; let them come out of the Chaldeans' land. Be like male goats at the head of the flock.
changes.after: Flee from Babylon's midst; go out from the Chaldeans' land. Be like male goats at the head of the flock.
changes.reason: The qere צְאוּ is an imperative (“go out”), parallel to נֻדוּ (“flee”); “let them come out” follows the ketiv and breaks the address.

changes.before: I have made you small among the nations, despised among humankind.
changes.after: For look, I have made you small among the nations, despised among humankind.
changes.reason: The verse opens כִּי־הִנֵּה (“For look”), which the column renders elsewhere and which ties the verse to the summons before it; it had been dropped.

changes.before: Flee, wander far away, dwell in the depths, Hazor's inhabitants—YHWH's declaration—for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has planned counsel against you and devised a purpose against them.
changes.after: Flee, wander far away, dwell in the depths, Hazor's inhabitants—YHWH's declaration—for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has planned counsel against you and devised a purpose against you.
changes.reason: The qere עֲלֵיכֶם (“against you”), as in the parallel clause, is the reading the column otherwise follows; “against them” follows the ketiv.

changes.before: Therefore my heart murmurs for Moab like flutes, and my heart murmurs for Kir-heres's men like flutes; therefore the wealth he gained has perished.
changes.after: Therefore my heart murmurs for Moab like flutes, and my heart murmurs for the men of Kir-heres like flutes; therefore the wealth he gained has perished.
changes.reason: “Kir-heres’s men” trips the ear; “the men of Kir-heres” matches the source’s אַנְשֵׁי קִיר־חֶרֶשׂ and the column’s own wording in v. 31.

changes.before: Kerioth is captured and the strongholds seized. That day Moab's warriors' hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
changes.after: Kerioth is captured and the strongholds seized. On that day the heart of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
changes.reason: The stacked possessive “Moab’s warriors’ hearts” is hard to hear; the Hebrew’s repeated singular לֵב … כְּלֵב (“the heart … like the heart”) reads clearly and keeps the source’s echo.

changes.before: Micah the Morashtite was prophesying in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and said to all Judah's people: Thus says YHWH of hosts: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become heaps, and the house's mountain wooded high places.
changes.after: Micah the Morashtite was prophesying in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and said to all Judah's people: Thus says YHWH of hosts: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become heaps, and the mountain of the house wooded high places.
changes.reason: “The house’s mountain” is obscure aloud; “the mountain of the house” (הַר הַבַּיִת, the Temple mount) is the familiar phrase and keeps the literal sense.

changes.before: But Ahikam son of Shaphan's hand was with Jeremiah, so that he was not given into the people's hand to be put to death.
changes.after: But the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so that he was not given into the people's hand to be put to death.
changes.reason: The possessive on “Shaphan’s hand” sounds as if the hand were Shaphan’s; “the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan” follows יַד אֲחִיקָם בֶּן־שָׁפָן and is clear aloud.

changes.before: I made the earth, the people, and the animals upon the earth's face by My great power and My outstretched arm, and I give it to whoever is right in My eyes.
changes.after: I made the earth, the people, and the animals upon the earth's face by My great power and My outstretched arm, and I give it to whomever it seems right in My eyes.
changes.reason: לַאֲשֶׁר יָשַׁר בְּעֵינָי is impersonal (“to whom it is right in My eyes”): the giving is what seems right to God, not the recipient who is upright, which matters as the next verse names Nebuchadnezzar.

changes.before: Look, YHWH's storm has gone out in fury, a sweeping tempest; it whirls upon the wicked's heads.
changes.after: Look, YHWH's storm has gone out in fury, a sweeping tempest; it whirls upon the head of the wicked.
changes.reason: “The wicked’s heads” is awkward aloud; עַל רֹאשׁ רְשָׁעִים is “upon the head of the wicked”, singular head, the familiar idiom.

changes.before: not like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took their hand to bring them out of Egypt's land—a covenant they broke, although I was their husband—YHWH's declaration.
changes.after: not like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took their hand to bring them out of Egypt's land—My covenant, which they broke, although I was their husband—YHWH's declaration.
changes.reason: The Hebrew says הֵפֵרוּ אֶת־בְּרִיתִי, “they broke My covenant”; “a covenant” loses that it was God’s own covenant they broke.

changes.before: The Chaldeans fighting this city will come, set this city on fire, and burn it, along with the houses whose roofs they used to burn incense to Baal and pour out libations to other gods to provoke Me.
changes.after: The Chaldeans fighting this city will come, set this city on fire, and burn it, along with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out libations to other gods to provoke Me.
changes.reason: As written the clause is ungrammatical (“houses whose roofs they used to burn incense”); “on whose roofs” renders עַל־גַּגּוֹתֵיהֶם and makes the sentence hold together aloud.

changes.before: Jonadab son of Rechab's words were upheld: he commanded his sons not to drink wine, and to this day they have drunk none, because they obey their father's command. Yet I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not obeyed Me.
changes.after: The words of Jonadab son of Rechab were upheld: he commanded his sons not to drink wine, and to this day they have drunk none, because they obey their father's command. Yet I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not obeyed Me.
changes.reason: “Jonadab son of Rechab’s words” sounds as if the words were Rechab’s; “the words of Jonadab son of Rechab” follows דִּבְרֵי יְהוֹנָדָב בֶּן־רֵכָב.

changes.before: All the women left in Judah's king's house are being brought out to Babylon's king's officials. They are saying, Your trusted friends misled you and prevailed over you. Your feet sank into the mire; they turned back.
changes.after: All the women left in the house of Judah's king are being brought out to the officials of Babylon's king. They are saying, Your trusted friends misled you and prevailed over you. Your feet sank into the mire; they turned back.
changes.reason: Two stacked double possessives in one sentence (“Judah’s king’s house … Babylon’s king’s officials”) are hard to follow aloud; the “of” forms follow the Hebrew construct chains.

changes.before: that you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you sent me to YHWH your God, saying, Pray for us to YHWH our God; tell us everything YHWH our God says, and we will do it.
changes.after: For you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you sent me to YHWH your God, saying, Pray for us to YHWH our God; tell us everything YHWH our God says, and we will do it.
changes.reason: The verse opens with causal כִּי (“for”); the dangling “that” after a full stop reads as a fragment and hides the reason Jeremiah gives.

changes.before: There will be no fugitive or survivor of Judah's remnant who came to reside there in Egypt's land to return to Judah's land, where they long to return and live. They will not return except fugitives.
changes.after: There will be no fugitive or survivor of Judah's remnant who came to reside there in Egypt's land, none to return to Judah's land, where they long to return and live. They will not return except fugitives.
changes.reason: Aloud, “came to reside there … to return” sounds as if they came in order to return; the Hebrew lists a second negated item (no survivor “to return”), so “none to return” keeps the sense clear.

changes.before: Is it nothing to you, all who pass along the road? Look and see whether there is pain like my pain, which was dealt to me, with which YHWH afflicted me on the day of His burning anger.
changes.after: May it not come upon you, all who pass along the road! Look and see whether there is pain like my pain, which was dealt to me, with which YHWH afflicted me on the day of His burning anger.
changes.reason: Rashi (following the Talmud, Sanhedrin 104b) reads לוֹא אֲלֵיכֶם as a wish, “may it not come to you”, the source of the phrase “not upon you”; the column follows the rabbinic reading where the Hebrew is ambiguous.

changes.before: Though He causes grief, He will have compassion according to His abundant steadfast love.
changes.after: For though He causes grief, He will have compassion according to His abundant steadfast love.
changes.reason: Verses 31–33 each open with כִּי; restoring “For” keeps the source’s threefold chain of reasons, as the column already does in 3:31 and 3:33.

changes.before: My enemies hunted me like a bird without cause.
changes.after: Those who were my enemies without cause hunted me down like a bird.
changes.reason: חִנָּם qualifies “my enemies” (enemies for no reason), but at the end of the line it sounds as if the bird were “without cause”; “hunted me down” also keeps the intensifying צוֹד צָדוּנִי.

changes.before: The iniquity of the daughter of my people became greater than Sodom's sin, which was overthrown in a moment, with no hands writhing over it.
changes.after: The iniquity of the daughter of my people became greater than Sodom's sin, which was overthrown in a moment, and no hands were laid upon it.
changes.reason: וְלֹא־חָלוּ בָהּ יָדָיִם means no hands came upon Sodom (Rashi: no human enemy fought against it; it fell at once); “hands writhing over it” obscures that point.

changes.before: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, those dwelling by the River Chebar, and where they were dwelling there; I sat there seven days, appalled among them.
changes.after: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, those dwelling by the River Chebar. I sat where they were dwelling, and I sat there seven days, appalled among them.
changes.reason: Follows the qere וָאֵשֵׁב (“and I sat where they dwelt”), the reading of Targum and Rashi; the current clause omits the first “I sat” and trips aloud.

changes.before: The food you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; eat it from time to time.
changes.after: The food you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; eat it at fixed times.
changes.reason: מֵעֵת עַד־עֵת means at a fixed interval (Rashi: once in each twenty-four hours); in modern English “from time to time” means occasionally, which says something the source does not.

changes.before: Drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; drink it from time to time.
changes.after: Drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; drink it at fixed times.
changes.reason: As in 4:10, מֵעֵת עַד־עֵת is a fixed interval (Rashi: once in twenty-four hours), not “occasionally”.

changes.before: She will not be a pot for you, and you will be meat within her. At Israel’s border I will judge you.
changes.after: She will not be a pot for you, nor will you be meat within her. At Israel’s border I will judge you.
changes.reason: The negative governs both halves (“nor will you be the meat in it”, as Rashi and Targum read it); the current English affirms that they will be the meat, the opposite of the verse.

changes.before: Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says Lord YHWH: I have put an end to this proverb; they will no longer use it as a proverb in Israel.’ Instead, speak to them: ‘The days have drawn near, and the word of every vision.
changes.after: Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says Lord YHWH: I have put an end to this proverb; they will no longer use it as a proverb in Israel.’ Instead, speak to them: ‘The days have drawn near, and so has the word of every vision.
changes.reason: “And the word of every vision” is left hanging aloud; the Hebrew means that the fulfilment of every vision is near too, which “and so has” makes clear without adding content.

changes.before: Therefore speak with them and say to them, ‘Thus says Lord YHWH: Anyone of the house of Israel who raises his idols upon his heart, sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet—I, YHWH, will answer him through it, according to the multitude of his idols,
changes.after: Therefore speak with them and say to them, ‘Thus says Lord YHWH: Anyone of the house of Israel who raises his idols upon his heart, sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet—I, YHWH, will answer him as he comes, according to the multitude of his idols,
changes.reason: Follows the qere בָא (“as he comes”) rather than the ketiv בה (“through it”), as the column does with qere readings elsewhere in Ezekiel.

changes.before: You did not walk in their ways or practice their abominations. In a little while, you acted more corruptly than they in all your ways.
changes.after: Was it not enough that you walked in their ways and practiced their abominations? In a little while, you acted more corruptly than they in all your ways.
changes.reason: וְלֹא בְדַרְכֵיהֶן הָלַכְתְּ means “not only in their ways did you walk” (Rashi: walking in their ways was not enough for you); the current English says she did not follow them at all, the opposite of the verse.

changes.before: He has withdrawn his hand from the poor, not taken interest or increase, carried out My judgments and walked in My statutes. He will not die for his father’s iniquity; he will surely live.
changes.after: He has held back his hand from harming the poor, not taken interest or increase, carried out My judgments and walked in My statutes. He will not die for his father’s iniquity; he will surely live.
changes.reason: מֵעָנִי הֵשִׁיב יָדוֹ means he kept his hand off the poor (Targum: from oppressing the poor); in English “withdrawn his hand from the poor” sounds as if he refused them help.

changes.before: I will purge from you the rebels and those transgressing against Me. I will bring them out of the land where they sojourn, but no one will enter Israel’s soil. You will know that I am YHWH.
changes.after: I will purge from you the rebels and those transgressing against Me. I will bring them out of the land where they sojourn, but they will not enter Israel’s soil. You will know that I am YHWH.
changes.reason: The subject of לֹא יָבוֹא is the rebels just purged, not everyone; “no one will enter” says that nobody at all will return, which the source does not say.

changes.before: All the sky’s birds will settle upon its fallen trunk, and all the field’s animals were upon its branches,
changes.after: All the sky’s birds will settle upon its fallen trunk, and all the field’s animals will be upon its branches,
changes.reason: The perfect הָיוּ stands in parallel with the imperfect יִשְׁכְּנוּ and describes the same scene of the felled tree; “will settle … were” makes the time jump backwards aloud.

changes.before: At the sound of its fall I shook nations when I brought it down to Sheol with those descending to the pit. In the lower land all Eden’s trees, the choice and best of Lebanon, all drinking water, were comforted.
changes.after: At the sound of its fall I shook nations when I brought it down to Sheol with those descending to the pit. In the lower land all Eden’s trees, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted.
changes.reason: כָּל־שֹׁתֵי מָיִם means the trees that drink water (as in 31:14); “all drinking water” is heard aloud as a noun phrase about water itself.

changes.before: For thus says Lord YHWH: Babylon’s king’s sword will come upon you.
changes.after: For thus says Lord YHWH: The sword of the king of Babylon will come upon you.
changes.reason: The stacked possessive “Babylon’s king’s sword” trips aloud; “the king of Babylon” is the column’s own wording in 30:10 and 30:24–25.

changes.before: There are all the north’s princes and all the Sidonians, who descended with the slain, ashamed of their terror from their might. They lay uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bore their shame with those descending to the pit.
changes.after: There are all the north’s princes and all the Sidonians, who descended with the slain, put to shame for all the terror their might had caused. They lay uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bore their shame with those descending to the pit.
changes.reason: בְּחִתִּיתָם מִגְבוּרָתָם בּוֹשִׁים is concessive (for all the terror caused by their might, they are put to shame); “ashamed of their terror from their might” is garbled and suggests they repented of spreading terror.

changes.before: They come to you as people come, and My people sit before you. They hear your words but do not do them, for they perform love with their mouths while their heart follows their unjust gain.
changes.after: They come to you as people come, and My people sit before you. They hear your words but do not do them, for with their mouths they show love, while their heart follows their unjust gain.
changes.reason: עֲגָבִים בְּפִיהֶם הֵמָּה עֹשִׂים is lovers’ talk made only with the mouth (cf. “love song” in 33:32); “perform love” sounds odd or sexual when read aloud.

changes.before: As you rejoiced over Israel’s house’s inheritance because it was desolate, so I will do to you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir and all Edom, all of it, and they will know that I am YHWH.’”
changes.after: As you rejoiced over the inheritance of Israel’s house because it was desolate, so I will do to you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir and all Edom, all of it, and they will know that I am YHWH.’”
changes.reason: The double possessive “Israel’s house’s inheritance” is hard to follow aloud; no change in meaning.

changes.before: therefore you will no longer devour human beings or make your nations stumble, declares Lord YHWH.
changes.after: therefore you will no longer devour human beings or bereave your nations, declares Lord YHWH.
changes.reason: Follows the qere תְשַׁכְּלִי (“bereave”), the reading of the Masoretic tradition, which answers the charge of 36:13 (“have bereaved your nations”); “stumble” renders the ketiv תכשלי.

changes.before: The side chambers stood chamber against chamber, three and thirty times. They entered into the wall belonging to the house for the side chambers all around, so as to be attached, but they were not to be attached within the house's wall.
changes.after: The side chambers stood chamber against chamber, thirty-three times. They entered into the wall belonging to the house for the side chambers all around, so as to be attached, but they were not to be attached within the house's wall.
changes.reason: “Three and thirty” is archaic word order that trips a modern listener; the column gives compound numbers in modern order elsewhere (e.g., “twenty-five”).

changes.before: Opposite the twenty belonging to the inner courtyard and opposite the paving belonging to the outer courtyard was gallery facing gallery, in three tiers.
changes.after: Opposite the twenty cubits belonging to the inner courtyard and opposite the paving belonging to the outer courtyard was gallery facing gallery, in three tiers.
changes.reason: הָעֶשְׂרִים is the twenty-cubit space of 41:10; aloud “the twenty” is left without any referent, and the unit is implied as throughout the measurements.

changes.before: Linen headdresses shall be on their heads and linen undergarments on their hips. They shall not gird themselves in a way that causes sweat.
changes.after: Linen headdresses shall be on their heads and linen undergarments on their hips. They shall not gird themselves where they sweat.
changes.reason: בַּיָּזַע is the place of sweat: the Talmud (Zevachim 18b) and Rashi explain that the sash is not tied at the loins or armpits where one sweats, not that the girding itself causes sweat.

changes.before: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a festival of weeks of days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
changes.after: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a festival of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
changes.reason: שְׁבֻעוֹת יָמִים here is a week of days (Rashi, Targum: a festival of seven days, as 45:23 confirms); “a festival of weeks” is heard aloud as Shavuot, which the verse does not mean.

changes.before: In the four corners of the courtyard were enclosed courts, forty long and thirty wide; all four corner courts had one measure.
changes.after: In the four corners of the courtyard were unroofed courts, forty long and thirty wide; all four corner courts had one measure.
changes.reason: The Mishnah (Middot 2:5) explains קְטֻרוֹת as courts that were not roofed, and Rashi follows it; the column prefers the rabbinic reading where the Hebrew is uncertain.

changes.before: youths without any defect, handsome, discerning in every kind of wisdom, possessing knowledge and understanding learning, and able to stand in the king’s palace, to teach them the writing and language of the Chaldeans.
changes.after: youths without any defect, handsome, discerning in every kind of wisdom, possessing knowledge, understanding learning, and able to stand in the king’s palace—and he was to teach them the writing and language of the Chaldeans.
changes.reason: וּלֲלַמְּדָם is the king’s order to Ashpenaz to teach the youths; as read, “able … to teach them” sounds as if the youths would do the teaching, and the run-on list blurs the separate qualities.

changes.before: To these four youths God gave knowledge and discernment in every kind of writing and wisdom, and Daniel understood every vision and dreams.
changes.after: To these four youths God gave knowledge and discernment in every kind of writing and wisdom, and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
changes.reason: “every vision and dreams” trips the ear; הֵבִין בְּכָל־חָזוֹן וַחֲלֹמוֹת is smoothed without changing its sense.

changes.before: This mystery was revealed to me because of no wisdom in me above all the living, but so that the interpretation might be made known to the king and you might know your heart’s thoughts.
changes.after: As for me, this mystery was revealed to me not because of any wisdom in me more than in all the living, but so that the interpretation might be made known to the king and you might know your heart’s thoughts.
changes.reason: “because of no wisdom in me” is hard to follow aloud, and the emphatic וַאֲנָה (“as for me”) that contrasts Daniel with the king (2:29) was dropped.

changes.before: Dominion, honor, and kingship were given him, and all peoples, nations, and languages served him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed.
changes.after: Dominion, honor, and kingship were given him, and all peoples, nations, and languages will serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed.
changes.reason: יִפְלְחוּן is imperfect (“will serve”), a lasting outcome of the grant, not a completed past act.

changes.before: He gave understanding, spoke with me, and said, “Daniel, I have now come out to give you insight and understanding.
changes.after: He gave me understanding, spoke with me, and said, “Daniel, I have now come out to give you insight and understanding.
changes.reason: וַיָּבֶן is causative “he made [me] understand” (Rashi); without “me” the phrase dangles when read aloud.

changes.before: At the appointed time he will return and enter the south, but it will not be as before or afterward.
changes.after: At the appointed time he will return and enter the south, but this latter time will not be like the first.
changes.reason: כָרִאשֹׁנָה וְכָאַחֲרֹנָה compares this last campaign with the first (Rashi: this latter coming will not be like the first); “or afterward” adds a future time the Hebrew does not mention.

changes.before: She conceived again and bore a daughter. He said to him, “Name her Lo-ruhamah—Not Pitied—for I will no longer have compassion on Israel's house, but I will surely assign them their portion.
changes.after: She conceived again and bore a daughter. He said to him, “Name her Lo-ruhamah—Not Pitied—for I will no longer have compassion on Israel's house, that I should ever forgive them.
changes.reason: כִּי־נָשֹׂא אֶשָּׂא לָהֶם is read by Rashi as forgiving (bearing their iniquity), continuing the refusal of compassion; “assign them their portion” has no basis in the Hebrew or the classical commentators.

changes.before: For they sow wind and will reap a whirlwind. It has no standing grain; the sprout produces no flour. Even if it produces any, foreigners will swallow it.
changes.after: For they sow wind and will reap a whirlwind. The standing grain has no head; it produces no flour. Even if it produces any, foreigners will swallow it.
changes.reason: קָמָה אֵין־לוֹ צֶמַח says the standing grain has no growth in it, not that there is no standing grain; the fix keeps the repeated “produces” (יַעֲשֶׂה) of the next line.

changes.before: What will you do on the appointed gathering's day, on the day of YHWH's festival?
