changes.after: What will you do on the day of the appointed gathering, on the day of YHWH's festival?
changes.reason: “The appointed gathering’s day” trips the ear; “on the day of … on the day of” is clearer aloud and restores the Hebrew’s parallel לְיוֹם … וּלְיוֹם.

changes.before: Behold, I am pressing down beneath you as the cart presses down that is full of sheaves.
changes.after: Behold, I am pressing down beneath you as the cart that is full of sheaves presses down.
changes.reason: Moving “that is full of sheaves” next to “the cart” keeps it from sounding aloud as if the pressing were full of sheaves.

changes.before: Do not look on your brother's day, the day of his calamity; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not boast on the day of distress.
changes.after: Do not look on your brother's day, the day of his calamity; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not open your mouth wide on the day of distress.
changes.reason: וְאַל־תַּגְדֵּל פִּיךָ is literally “do not make your mouth great”; keep the source’s image of the gaping, jeering mouth rather than the abstract “boast”.

changes.before: Do not enter My people's gate on the day of their disaster. Do not you too look on his misery on the day of his disaster, and do not reach out for his wealth on the day of his disaster.
changes.after: Do not enter My people's gate on the day of their disaster. You too, do not look on his misery on the day of his disaster, and do not reach out for his wealth on the day of his disaster.
changes.reason: “Do not you too look” trips the ear; reordering keeps גַם־אַתָּה (“you too”) and the meaning.

changes.before: The men feared YHWH greatly. They offered a sacrifice to YHWH and made vows.
changes.after: The men were filled with great fear of YHWH. They offered a sacrifice to YHWH and made vows.
changes.reason: וַיִּירְאוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים יִרְאָה גְדוֹלָה repeats 1:10 word for word, now directed at YHWH; render it as 1:10 does so the deliberate echo is heard.

changes.before: Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all. In Beth-leaphrah I have rolled myself in dust.
changes.after: Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all. In Beth-leaphrah roll yourself in dust.
changes.reason: The English follows the Ketiv התפלשתי (“I have rolled”); the Masoretic reading (Qere) is the imperative הִתְפַּלָּשִׁי addressed to Beth-leaphrah, as the column follows elsewhere.

changes.before: On that day someone will take up a taunt against you and lament a mournful lament: ‘We are utterly ruined! He changes the portion of My people. How He takes it away from me! To a turncoat He divides our fields.’
changes.after: On that day someone will take up a taunt against you and lament a mournful lament: ‘We are utterly ruined! He changes the portion of my people. How He takes it away from me! To a turncoat He divides our fields.’
changes.reason: חֵלֶק עַמִּי is spoken by the lamenting Israelite (‘We are utterly ruined… from me… our fields’), not by God; capital “My” wrongly makes it God’s speech.

changes.before: Hear this now, heads of Jacob's house and rulers of Israel's house, who abhor justice and twist everything straight,
changes.after: Hear this now, heads of Jacob's house and rulers of Israel's house, who abhor justice and twist all that is straight,
changes.reason: “twist everything straight” can be heard as “straighten everything”; וְאֵת כָּל־הַיְשָׁרָה יְעַקֵּשׁוּ means they make crooked all that is straight.

changes.before: The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says YHWH of hosts, and in this place I will give peace, declares YHWH of hosts.”
changes.after: The glory of this latter house will be greater than that of the former, says YHWH of hosts, and in this place I will give peace, declares YHWH of hosts.”
changes.reason: Following Rashi (and Bava Batra 3a), הָאַחֲרוֹן qualifies the house: the glory of this latter (Second) house will exceed that of the former house.

changes.before: How great his goodness and beauty! Grain will make young men flourish, and new wine virgins.
changes.after: For how great his goodness, and how great his beauty! Grain will make young men flourish, and new wine virgins.
changes.reason: The Hebrew opens with כִּי and repeats מַה (ki mah tuvo u-mah yofyo, “for how great … and how great …”); the English dropped both the “for” and the second exclamation.

changes.before: I shepherded the flock destined for slaughter, therefore the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs: I called one Pleasantness and the other Bonds, and I shepherded the flock.
changes.after: I shepherded the flock destined for slaughter, for the sake of the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs: I called one Pleasantness and the other Bonds, and I shepherded the flock.
changes.reason: “Therefore the afflicted of the flock” cannot be followed aloud; Rashi glosses לָכֵן here as “for the sake of” the poor of the flock.

changes.before: YHWH will go out and fight against those nations, as on a day when He fights on a day of battle.
changes.after: YHWH will go out and fight against those nations, as on the day He fought, on a day of battle.
changes.reason: כְּיוֹם הִלָּחֲמוֹ points to a past day of His fighting (Rashi: as He fought at the Sea of Reeds); “a day when He fights” made it a general present and repeated “on a day” awkwardly.

changes.before: May YHWH cut off from the tents of Jacob, for the man who does this, the one who is awake and the one who answers, and the one who presents an offering to YHWH of hosts.
changes.after: May YHWH cut off from the man who does this, from the tents of Jacob, the one who is awake and the one who answers, and the one who presents an offering to YHWH of hosts.
changes.reason: לָאִישׁ means those are cut off from the man (the Talmud, Sanhedrin 82a, followed by Rashi: he will have no one of his left awake among the sages or answering among the disciples); “for the man” sounded aloud as if the cutting off were done on his behalf.
